notes: §1985:XII.2.4 GR12: "The text produced as a result of the complete processing of a COPY statement must not contain a COPY statement." ResolveOneCopy asks FindStatementKeyword whether the library text holds a COPY statement and, below 2002, refuses it at the outer COPY through the constructs row copy-nested-library-text-2002 (COBOL0900); the other way the produced text can hold one, a REPLACING operand that introduces COPY, is ApplyReplacements' ForbiddenIn (COBOL2574, every edition). A REPLACING phrase can neither write nor remove the word COPY of library text (the 1985 text-word excludes the word 'COPY', §1985:III.2 (3), so no pseudo-text holds it, and §1985:XII.2.3 SR6 excludes it as word-1 or word-2), so the library text and the produced text differ only in what is a comment-entry: the converter of the library text (NormalizeCopybookMapped) is handed the spelling the phrase gives a word (ParagraphWordAsReplaced) and reads a comment-entry paragraph in the REPLACED text, whose COPY is part of the comment-entry (§1985:XII.2.3 SR10). Probes at --std 85: PLACEHOLDER. COPY PB5732Z. copied under REPLACING ==PLACEHOLDER== BY ==AUTHOR== runs (X=3) and the same library text under a REPLACING that matches nothing is COBOL0900; the witness PB5126OU holds COPY PB5126IN is refused. A REPLACE statement of the source text that writes the header word leaves its COPY a COPY statement, as it must: REPLACE is processed after every COPY (§1985:XII.3.4 GR4), so the header is not yet a comment-entry paragraph when the COPY is processed. kb/Work PB5732. retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Preprocessor/ReferenceFormatProcessor.cs#IsCommentEntryParagraph (the extract of ReferenceFormatProcessor (kb/Work PB2328): the member moved verbatim to the file of the type that holds it now (LogicalLineConverter, FixedFormConverter, FreeFormConverter, LogicalLineBuilder); the same code)

next.reason: 1985 (1993 amendment): 'The text produced as a result of the complete processing of a COPY statement must not contain a COPY statement', so no copied text may hold a COPY. 2023 is looser. §2023:7.2.3.3 SR1 allows a COPY statement 'in source text or in library text'. §2023:7.2.3.4 GR12 says 'If the REPLACING phrase is not specified, the library text may contain a COPY statement that does not include a REPLACING phrase', and requires support for at least 5 nesting levels. The bar remains only where §2023:7.2.3.4 GR10 applies ('If the REPLACING phrase is specified, the library text shall not contain a COPY statement') and where §2023:7.2.3.4 GR13 applies ('The replacing action of a COPY statement shall not introduce a COPY statement'). A program 1985 must refuse, nested COPY without REPLACING, is legal in 2023. Both editions check this at compile time; no exception condition is involved.
